chunks.text: Teak (Tectona grandis) is a large deciduous tree in the family Lamiaceae (the mint family, which also contains basil and lavender) — not, as often assumed, a member of the walnut or mahogany families. The genus Tectona has only three species in total, of which teak is by far the most widespread and commercially important. It is native to South and Southeast Asia, chiefly Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Sri Lanka and Thailand; molecular studies identify two natural genetic centres, one in India and one spanning Myanmar and Laos, with Myanmar alone holding close to half of the world's remaining natural teak forest. The tree can reach 40 m in height, with grey to greyish-brown bark and large, rough, ovate-elliptic leaves 15-45 cm long with hairy undersides. It bears small, fragrant white flowers in dense branched clusters (panicles) from June to August, pollinated mainly by bees. Teak favours mixed hardwood forest with 1,250-1,650 mm of annual rainfall but tolerates a much wider range (500-5,000 mm), and is currently assessed as Endangered by the IUCN owing to deforestation pressure on natural stands even though plantation-grown teak is abundant.

Teak's heartwood is yellowish to golden-brown, smells faintly of leather when freshly milled, darkens further with age, and has a density around 660 kg/m3 at 15% moisture. Its combination of high natural oil content, high tensile strength and tight, straight grain gives it exceptional resistance to rot, moisture and insect attack without chemical treatment, which is why it has been used in shipbuilding and boat decking for over 2,000 years and remains prized today for outdoor furniture, flooring and interior trim. Almost all commercial teak now comes from plantations rather than natural forest — Indonesia's state-run Perum Perhutani is a major producer, and India's Nilambur region (Kerala) is home to what is described as the world's oldest teak plantation, established in the 1840s. Culinary use is minor but real: in South India teak leaves are used to wrap and steam jackfruit dumplings (pellakai gatti), and in Indonesia they wrap gudeg (jackfruit curry).

Teak has notable cultural and record-setting associations: 49 teak beams reportedly form part of the roof structure of the Kaaba in Mecca. In August 2017, some of the largest living teak trees in the world were found in Homalin Township, Myanmar, the biggest measuring 8.4 m in girth; India's own celebrated Kannimara teak specimen (in Kerala's Parambikulam forests) is estimated at 450-500 years old. Illegal logging remains a serious problem in parts of Myanmar, with a large share of unregulated teak reportedly crossing into China, prompting regulatory responses such as the EU Timber Regulation aimed at high-risk sourcing regions.
